notes.title: Patch Note 1.0.7
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/1c94bb3bc5b0ae22aff963286c3e85481f2be0e5.jpg[/img]

Dear Monarchs,

This update focuses on improving the quality of the Chinese and English translations, along with addressing various issues in the game.

[h3]Translation Quality Improvements
[/h3]
Corrected typos and awkward expressions in the Chinese and English translations to make them more natural.



[h2]Bug Fixes and Feature Improvements
[/h2]
[h3]Translation and Text
[/h3]
- Fixed an issue where tooltips and card texts were not displaying.
- Corrected inaccurate descriptions on certain cards.
- Fixed a bug where incorrect character names appeared in dialogue.

[h3]UI and Features[/h3]

- Improved the edge-scrolling feature for smoother movement when the mouse is near the edge of the screen.
- Fixed an issue where card keywords were not visible in the deck UI. (Pressing "K" now activates keywords.)
- Fixed a bug where ascended units remained in the queue after being ascended in the Ritual Altar UI.
- Resolved an issue where abnormal prisons could appear in the Prison UI.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

- Fixed an issue where certain building effects could block game progression.
- Resolved bugs related to building requisition.
- Fixed a bug where acquiring the Monarch Summoning Trait would remove existing summon effects.
- Added a feature to prevent duplicate rewards from being granted.
- Improved the stability of the save function.


Thank you to everyone who reported bugs! We will continue to work hard to provide a better gaming experience.

notes.title: Hotfix 1.0.6 Patch Note
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/d920e08e24ee53c94c9698ef427cca693b533d87.jpg[/img]

Dear Monarchs of the Dungeon,

I'm writing to update you with a 1.0.6 hotfix.

[h3]+ Fixed an A-class bug that prevented players from entering Round 7 after clearing Round 6 during Story Chapter 1 in some situations.
[/h3]

Besides, we've received a lot of great feedback since the game's release, and there are some things we haven't been able to address during the Early Access period, so we'd like to outline our plans going forward:

[h3] Upcoming Update Features :
[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improving the control sensor to move the screen when the mouse pointer is on the edge of the screen.
[*] Fixing the card keywords not showing up in the Deck UI.
[*] Working on localisation issues in the Simplified Chinese and English translations.
[*] Fixing for text displayed in tooltips or on cards not displaying correctly.
[*] Fixing for incorrect character display in some dialogue.
[*] Fixing an issue where gaining the Monarch Summon-related Perk would cause existing summons to lose their effect.
[*] Preventing rewards from being duplicated.
[/list]


[h3]Issues currently identified, and in the process of being fixed :
[/h3]

[list]
[*] Work is underway on controller support.
[*] Adding input info for using secondary actions or features in each UI will be added.
[*] The Prison UI is being fixed for spawning incorrect prisoners.
[*] We are fixing an issue in the Ritual Altar UI where units could remain in the queue after being ascended.
[*] We're working on a fix for situations where tooltips would not activate and deactivate correctly.
[*] We are fixing a situation where combat acceleration was not being applied correctly.
[*] We're working on an issue in the Construction UI where some tile selections become unavailable in certain situations.
[*] Working on improvements to the save function.
[*] Fixing a bug with building conscription.

We look forward to improving the game and making sure you have a great experience.

Best Regards,

Minho,
Dvora Studio.

notes.title: FULL RELEASED
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/ccf687107843960c53a31242dedc1c0885d3d5a7.jpg[/img]

[i]Dear Monarchs,[/i]

Vambrace Dungeon Monarch is finally released! 

[previewyoutube=nKU7Y-arzrk;full][/previewyoutube]

Today, developer Dvora Studio and publisher Headup are pleased to announce the release of Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch, their fantasy deckbuilding, tactical, auto-battler, available now via Steam.

Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch challenges you to utilize your strategic deck of cards to unleash devastating magic spells and summon formidable combat units onto the battlefield. Annihilate your foes with lightning bolts, fireballs, and barrages of arrows while buffing your troops with damage boosts, morale boons, and protective armor. Observe as your units join the battle, decimating intruders with unique abilities.

In this full release update, you'll find a complete story in two parts, a new Freeplay mode separated by a hard mode, and a number of gameplay enhancements and user-friendliness improvements based on feedback from EA. (We apologise for not being able to implement all of your feedback, but we did the best we could with the resources we had, and there will be more updates in the future.)
Now you can see the game in its entirety. We hope you enjoy it. Join Phenix (the main character) or M5 on their journey!

Best Regards,

Minho Kim,
Dvora Studio.

notes.title: ⚔️ Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch Update 0.2.0.7 Launched!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/c6f2a1c634c1b1a6a0ea331273997412a916bdfd.jpg[/img]

Greetings, Dungeon Monarchs.

We recently released update 0.2.07 for Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch. This update takes into account the feedback we've received from gamers who've purchased the game, as well as various improvement ideas, and addresses some of the negative feedback we've received. Below are the details of the update:

1. Finalised Save System: We've improved the save system so that you can now autosave in Freeplay mode and manually save in Story mode. We've also changed the game so that if you're in Story mode and Gameover, you can still go back to the previous stage and try again. This gives you the opportunity to try again rather than give up.

2. We finally added a Skip button to video cutscenes. This allows you to move on if you've seen the video again.

3. The first Simplified Chinese localization is now live. We've had some great responses to the game in China and requests for Chinese, so we're hoping to get more diverse gamers to come and give us feedback on the game. It's not perfect, but we'll try to get it checked by native speakers soon.


March is coming! We've got a lot of improvements and additions planned for the month of March that we think you'll enjoy. We'll be improving content for upgrades and building construction, as well as releasing the full story part 1. We'll also be releasing a separate tutorial for the mod changes, so stay tuned for that. Thank you.

Minho,
Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #7: Two Games, One Universe
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/4431a62a9aa28ccf4bd609f19044625da26141bc.jpg[/img]

Happy Monday, Dungeon Monarchs!
 
We know that a lot of you out there were fans of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/904380/Vambrace_Cold_Soul/]Vambrace: Cold Soul[/url], and you are wondering how exactly Dungeon Monarch is going to feature the world and lore of the Vambrace universe. After all, it is a completely different style of game than Cold Soul. 
 
But there are some things we can share without spoiling the story of Dungeon Monarch!
 
First of all, we return to the world of Ethera! You will realise soon into the journey that the eponymous Dungeon is, in fact, located on the continent of Edena. This is the continent of human culture in the world of the Vambrace. Humans from the continent of Edena are referred to as Edeni, of which you will meet plenty on your journey, and you may remember that Evelia Lyric (the heroine of Cold Soul) was Edeni. 
 
On the continent of Edena there exists an expansive human empire, with many different free cities, each with their own goals and ambitions. You will both come up against, and ally with, characters from many of these cities and there will be some familiar faces from the Cold Souls world ... but we won’t say any more on that front, so that you can discover this for yourself.
 
Finally, if you played Cold Soul, you will be right at home among many familiar terms that are shared across the world of Ethera. All of the races you came to know and love are here: from Human to Sylvani Elf to Drow to Foxier to Dwarf, and even the alien race of the Archons.
 
... okay, okay! We will give you one tiny spoiler. You will once again meet the Guardians from the Alliance in Dungeon Monarch, but this time from a much different perspective than you may remember from Cold Soul. This time around they are dangerous, powerful, and are eager to crush the player’s Dungeon. Maybe you’re not going to be on the side you thought you were?
 
Well, there's not too much time left until you can find out tomorrow! Until then, please do us a favor and click on "Follow" as well as "Add To Your Wishlist". That would really help us a lot. ❤️
 
Have a great start into the new week all!
Minho & Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #6: Let's talk about "Roguelike"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/654539a700f8f28c296d71f4f87714ed9e785067.jpg[/img]

Greetings, Dungeon Monarchs!

There are many roguelike game genres out there. Extreme replayability and randomization, game situations that change every time you play again and again, and high difficulty levels that are not easily solved on the first try...

Without unlockables and specialized skill techniques over multiple play-throughs, it's hard to beat the game and see the ending. But this genre has the advantage of being enjoyable for a long time. If you don't get bored, of course.

But in a way, I personally don't like the idea of constant failure and replayability for "one step forward". All of our games have some sort of narrative structure to them, and the narrative has an introduction, it has an arc, and it requires the player to successfully navigate through what's come before in order to get to the conclusion.

So the roguelike genre is actually something we don't do very often (even though some of the team really enjoy it), and we've learned a lot from our previous game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/904380/Vambrace_Cold_Soul/]Vambrace: Cold Soul[/url].

The difficulty curve in this game is also designed to not encourage players to fail, and we're hoping that after a long battle, you'll achieve something in this dungeon. Of course, there's a lot of randomness that keeps the game from becoming repetitive, but it's entirely up to the player to try out different legion (synergy) combinations to keep the game fresh. (In other words, it's a game where we want the player's choices to enrich the game). 

Regardless, it's a game with rogue-elements. However, I would like to point out to players that there is the main dish out of the genre, and it can be eaten multiple times, because the rouge-lite sauces are varied to make the main dish delicious.

That's it for the "roguelike" part of Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch! Next time I will tell you more about the Monarch. And if you like what you read (or have played with our demo), please do us a favour and click on "Follow" as well as "Add To Your Wishlist". That would really help us a lot. ❤️

Talk to you again really soon!
Minho & Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #5: Let's talk about "Auto Battler"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/435494c619d9c79f9d3d50ff71545d6659c486b7.jpg[/img]

Happy Friday, Dungeon Monarchs!

Teamfight Tactics (aka TFT) was my first exposure to Auto Battler as a genre, but its roots are known as DotA Auto Chess. I was personally vaguely aware of the genre and its mechanics, and never "really" played LoL (which is odd, considering my first company sponsored the LoL Champions League in Korea, and we used to use it to pay for lunch).
 
However, my brother Hyunho (aka KYNO), who is the game designer of this game, was an avid LoL player, as are a whole bunch of his friends. I was told I had to try TFT, so I played it, and I was introduced to the concept of "Synergy". Naturally, TFT got me hooked, and I was very interested in the unique ‘hands off but head on’ commander role.
 
In [b]Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch[/b], the army doesn't have to be told what to do by the Monarch (the player), but rather, they seek out and engage enemies on their own initiative. This part of the game is automatic. You, as a commander, either engage in an unfavourable battlefield or observe from afar, casting spells and creating environments. This doesn't mean that you can't direct your army. You need to deploy them in the right places to maximize "Synergy", which means that they become stronger when members of the same attribute are present on the field.

It's like a group of puppies barking and playing with each other more vigorously.

If your army has the Vampire attribute, it's important to keep a variety of Vampires on the field to maintain strength. If some of your cards have the ability to add a Vampire Synergy effect, that's even better! Keep in mind that placing multiple Vampires of a single unit doesn't increase Synergy - it needs to be a ‘bunch of different Vampires’ to amplify Vampire Synergy.

High Synergy scores add unique benefits of that army's attribute, so you'll want to use your judgement to keep your army alive with the high scores. It may seem like you're doing nothing, watching your soldiers move around automatically, but your commander-brain should be busy thinking!

That's it for the "auto battler" part of [b]Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch[/b]! Next time I will tell you more about the "roguelite" aspect. And if you like what you read (or have played with our demo), please do us a favour and click on "Follow" as well as "Add To Your Wishlist". That would really help us a lot. ❤️

Talk to you again really soon!
Minho & Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #4: Let's talk about "Deck-Building"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/175a18d9054b629a6e49601d397c08ae54e81e60.jpg[/img]

Greetings Dungeon Monarchs!

The topic of "deck-building" is a sensitive and difficult one to explain. Many games have already done great achievements with the genre, and those who play them have clear standards and definitions of what it is. There are variations on the theme, but the basic idea is that people want to have fun.
 
It's an important obligation of games in the "deck-building" genre to do this well, and to make sure that the gameplay behaviour is fun.
 
In this game, there are cards. There are two main types of cards: Regular Cards and The Monarch Cards. Regular Cards are randomly selected and appear at the bottom of the screen, defined as 'your Hand', every turn, and you can play them as long as you have energy. They can change the environment in the dungeon, trigger certain situations, or cast curses that affect enemies and allies.

The Monarch Cards can only be used when The Monarch, Dark Lord (You!), is on the field, and represent the magic, abilities, and skills used by the protagonist himself rather than environmental events. Both of these types of cards are randomly selected to come into your hand, so it's advantageous to have your main character on the field, preferably in command of the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/8bf5a44db25e95f6dd1cd538ea84d82d8275ac3d.jpg[/img]
 
As you know, the game doesn't just rely on cards to fend off enemies, you also have to mobilise your army to stop them from invading, and each army has different abilities and may fight better in certain environments. This is why your cards need to be carefully selected: you can only choose a limited number of cards to take part in defensive battles, so you need to think about which cards will give your current army an advantage. If you've assembled a bunch of fire-powered troops, and the only thing they do is flood the dungeon, that's not going to help you in battle.
 
If you find yourself struggling to keep your enemies at bay, and you're not getting much out of your cards, you should consider "rebuilding" your current deck. Your deck composition can turn the tide of battle, which is why deckbuilding is such an important aspect of this game.

That's it for the "deck-building" part of [b]Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch[/b]! Next time I will tell you more about the "auto battler" aspect. And if you like what you read (or have played with our demo), please do us a favour and click on "Follow" as well as "Add To Your Wishlist". That would really help us a lot. ❤️

Talk to you again really soon!

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #3: The Tasty Recipe of Dungeon Monarch
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/7b53e90fc8db010fb73600fd08164357088a59da.jpg[/img]

Greetings adventurers!

It's about time for the third issue of our "Into the Dungeon" update series. This time we are dealing with the tasty genre mix of [b]Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch[/b].

When talking about a game, discussing its genre is the easiest way to describe it. Each genre has an iconic gameplay style and gives players a general idea of what to expect. Many gamers are able to figure out ‘what this game is about’ the moment they know its genre, and can interpret whether they'll like it or not.

However, when it comes to interpreting a game called Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch, these genre descriptions seem to need more explanation, because the genres that describe the game are unfamiliar to each other, and the combination is both exotic and unclear. 

At its core, it is a "[i][b]Deck-building[/b][/i]" game. You have to create combinations of cards in a limited deck and utilise them to overcome challenges. The cards have different skills and effects, so you have to make sure you have the right mix of cards that will be useful in the current environment, and consider the best order and choice of cards that randomly pop up in your hand whenever a challenge arises.

This is where the genre of "[i][b]Auto-Battler[/b][/i]" comes in. The "environment" in which to prepare your cards is the legions of players currently residing in the dungeon. If you've created a dungeon full of vampires, the cards you need to play are those that favor the vampires. Conversely, if you've created a dungeon environment full of undead, you'll need to choose cards that favor the dead and endanger the living.

[previewyoutube=IVuRoFHei9c;full][/previewyoutube]
The challenge is that all of the unwanted visitors to your dungeon have been told by the outside world that they are heroes. Some of them may be unremarkable adventurers or thieves, but most of them are. They may be strong against certain factions, or infinitely weak in certain environments. They don't appear in any particular order, and your awesome Dark Legion may find itself in an unexpected crisis.

This is where cards come into play. If your army is a moving barrier to defend your dungeon, cards can be a sharp spear to incapacitate your enemies.

However, your dungeon has very few resources for all this brilliant strategy. The real owner of the dungeon is sealed away and asleep, and you, as regent, are barely keeping it fed. You can't choose all of the new cards or money-making opportunities that pop up from time to time, so you're forced to make one or two good choices and hope for the best. These different opportunities add to the roguelike aspect of the game.

Defending this dungeon and keeping the enemies at bay is a constant siege, which also leans towards the "[i][b]Defence[/b][/i]" genre. You'll need to make good use of the Monarch, the Dark Regent, who acts as your builder, as he'll be travelling around the dungeon and taking out enemies that your walls can't keep out.

The combination of genres may sound and look tricky, but once you get into it, you'll realize that it's not too difficult. There are familiar gameplay elements throughout, so don't be afraid to take on the challenge. The game has a high learning curve, but you'll enjoy it and before you know it, you'll be a notoriously powerful DARK LORD.

Talk to you again really soon!
Minho & Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #2: How the Vambrace Universe came into being!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/4aee00c844d22d2705ae63b209d2ee54522a6a94.jpg[/img]

Greetings adventurers!

Dungeon Monarch is the second game in the Vambrace universe that we are developing. But as the word “universe” implies: there is still room for more! But for now, let's dive into the past and look at how the Vambrace universe came to be.

I laid the foundation for it 26 years ago. But one thing at a time.

When I got into game development, I realized that I had the dream to bring stories and settings to life, one by one. My amazing friend and brilliant writer T.L. Riven went through them, and the story of Lyric in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/904380/Vambrace_Cold_Soul/]Vambrace: Cold Soul[/url] was the beginning of what the team would eventually create.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/91efec838404e6ef5634caa19f57f9dc7b77c6fc.png[/img]

I was thrilled to find out that the world of the game was so finely crafted, and I knew that I could build on the stories that had been hidden in the depths of my HDDs. Therefore, all of the fantasy stories that Dvora Studio has created, and will continue to create, are more or less based on this game world, which we call the Vambrace Saga.

From the creation of a world to its destruction, in its myriad chronicles lie countless villains and heroes whose names we still do not know, and in that order and chaos lie the adventures and challenges, the noble sacrifices and meaningful moments that Dvora Studio seeks to create.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/7166e78dcf614948fc1295903f6bbae5d6d27634.png[/img]
 
Some of our games have the word "Vambrace" in them, or are set in the world of the Vambrace Saga. This fantasy theme has a very special value for Dvora Studio, and for me as the founder. This fantasy world actually started back in 1998, when I was in the sixth grade of my elementary school, and started drawing pictures and making up stories with creative characters and creative episodes.

At the time, gaming culture was starting to develop in South Korea, and I was immersed in the graphics and themes of games like StarCraft, Genesis: Tempest, Tomb Raider 3, KKND2, Dune2000, Age of Empires, and many others. I used to draw various copycats and invented characters in my sketch books all day, and I used to make up crazy and weird stories to share with my classmates for fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/cde7044594df8b0f2d52efcfbb4baef3901b4f19.png[/img]

As I entered adolescence, the gap between the ideal and the reality became more and more obvious, and I used to relieve my academic stress and worries about the future with these creative and fun fantasy stories. I was fascinated by wonderful stories such as the Harry Potter series, the Lord of the Rings films, the Chronicles of Narnia, and other adventure tales, and I started to think: "I need to study to make a good story".

The more I drew, the more I realized that I didn't just love drawing, I loved creating the lives and stories of the characters in my drawings, so I studied more structured texts and settings to refine the stories and worlds I'd been creating since I was a kid, and as an adult, they've been piling up in my personal archive.

And you already guessed it: Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch is one of those stories.

Talk to you again really soon!
Minho & Dvora Studio

notes.title: ⚔️ Into the Dungeon #1: Meet Dungeon Monarch-Developer Dvora Studio!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/4cb30969ed886b459045b814a83e164c53d23202.jpg[/img]

Greetings Dungeon Monarchs!
 
Before releasing [b]Vambrace: Dungeon Monarch[/b] later this year, we want to tell you more about the game with our "Into the Dungeon" update series. But not only about the game, but also about us: Dvora Studio - the team behind titles like The Coma, Vambrace and Scarlet Hood.
 
Dvora Studio was created on the 28th August 2015, but I spent one year working in cafes in order to make the first game in the Coma Series. The formal company name was Devespresso Games (Dev + Espresso Coffee), as this was what shaped the first few years of the indie game development life. I changed the name to Dvora Studio later on, because it was easier to remember:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44946660/0e943aaf3176ffed675434cda52eff8ce880c7f3.png[/img]
 
Back then, we struggled to secure a programmer who can actually build the game. I’m a graphic artist with a bunch of cool stories, but I need to have someone who actually makes the games with me. Those seats were taken by two programmer friends, who were later replaced by my cousin, and eventually filled with three indie game programmers now.
 
To create the narrative stories and events, I requested custom modules and DB forms to shape the visuals of the games by myself for [b]Vambrace: Cold Soul[/b], [b]The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters[/b], and [b]Scarlet Hood and the Wickend Wood[/b]. It added a lot to my workload, but I think it was possible because I wasn't married with kids back then, because it was so rewarding to work day and night to get the game done and to share the story and the characters and the world with gamers.
 
T. L. Riven and KYNO have been a huge part of that journey. They've kept my imagination and inspiration flowing and helped me stay on track to keep making games. The stories that T. L. Riven has built on top of my ideas have been amazing and exciting, and he's gone on to do some amazing things as a game writer and is now a game producer for another company. KYNO is now a brand new game designer, designing and creating sophisticated and highly playable games.
 
I’m grateful that the games we make have been described by many as having 'unique artwork, beautiful music, and immersive, detailed worlds', which has led to a lot of people who love and remember these game worlds (The Coma Series & Vambrace Saga), and it's a pleasure to work for them.
 
Now I'm married, and I'm a dad with two babies to look after. Obviously, I look at the world differently, I have a different sense of purpose, and making a game with those experiences adds a different depth than before. I want to continue to make games that people remember. I want to make games for as long as I have the energy.
 
There are currently six developers working at the company, including myself, and we're braving the unbearably hot Korean summer weather. I know a lot of people are surprised at how six people can produce two game projects, but it's actually happening. We have a lot of ideas in our heads, and we can't wait to show them off.
 
Talk to you again really soon!
Minho & Dvora Studio
